title: God's final word: the better Son

passage.why: You asked for an overview of Hebrews and to unpack chapters 1 to 3 together. Hebrews is a sermon to tired believers tempted to drift: Jesus is better, so hold fast. It holds the New Testament's fullest word on Sabbath rest (4:9), so it suits Saturdays.

readAloud: Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed the heir of all things, through whom also he created the world. He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his nature, and he upholds the universe by the word of his power. After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high. (Hebrews 1:1-3)
setting: Hebrews calls itself 'my word of exhortation' (13:22): a sermon sent as a letter. The author is unknown. Paul, Barnabas (Tertullian's view), Apollos (Luther's view) and others have been proposed; Origen concluded only God knows (DISPUTED). It was most likely written in the AD 60s, before the temple fell in AD 70, to Jewish Christians who had suffered loss and prison (10:32-34) and were now tempted to drift back. The sermon alternates teaching about Christ with five warnings: 2:1-4, 3:7-4:13, 5:11-6:12, 10:26-39 and 12:25-29.

sections.heading: The shape of the book
sections.body: 1:1-2:18 the Son is greater than the angels. 3:1-4:13 greater than Moses, and the rest that remains. 4:14-7:28 the great high priest in the order of Melchizedek. 8:1-10:18 a better covenant, sanctuary and sacrifice, once for all. 10:19-12:29 draw near, hold fast, run with endurance. 13 love, hospitality, marriage, money, leaders. The backbone is Psalm 110: the Son seated at God's right hand (110:1) and a priest forever (110:4).

sections.heading: Chapter 1: seven claims, seven quotations
sections.body: The Son is heir of all things, agent of creation, the radiance of God's glory, the exact imprint of his nature, the one who upholds the universe, who made purification for sins, and who sat down. Then seven Old Testament quotations place him above the angels: Psalm 2:7, 2 Samuel 7:14, Deuteronomy 32:43, Psalm 104:4, Psalm 45:6-7 ('Your throne, O God'), Psalm 102:25-27 and Psalm 110:1. The Deuteronomy line matches a Dead Sea Scroll copy found at Qumran (4QDeut-q), which ties to your Biblical Timeline.

sections.heading: He sat down
sections.body: Old Testament priests stood daily, offering the same sacrifices that could never take away sins (10:11). Jesus sat down, because the work was finished (1:3; 10:12). That is the root of all rest in Hebrews.

sections.heading: Chapter 2: do not drift; we see Jesus
sections.body: 'We must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, lest we drift away from it' (2:1). Drift takes no effort, only neglect. Then Psalm 8: humanity was made to rule, but 'we do not yet see everything in subjection to him. But we see him... namely Jesus' (2:8-9). He shared our flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free those enslaved by the fear of death (2:14-15), and became a merciful and faithful high priest who helps the tempted (2:17-18).

sections.heading: Chapter 3: greater than Moses; today
sections.body: Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant; Jesus is faithful over it as a son (3:5-6). Then Psalm 95: 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.' The wilderness generation saw God's works for forty years and still did not trust him: 'they were unable to enter because of unbelief' (3:19). The cure is community: 'exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today' (3:13).

sections.heading: The warnings: three readings
sections.body: Arminian and Wesleyan readers hold that real believers can finally fall away. Many Reformed readers hold the warnings address those who never truly believed. Others (Schreiner and Caneday) read them as one of the means God uses to keep his people. All agree: take them seriously and hold fast. Worth an hour with your pastor.

observe: Hebrews 1:1-2: list each contrast between 'long ago' and 'these last days'.
Count the seven claims about the Son in 1:2-3. Which one moves you most, and why?
In 3:7-19, trace the words heart, today, rest and unbelief. What is the root problem?

words.note: The mark a seal or die leaves in wax or metal. Look at the Son and you see exactly what God is like.
Pioneer or trailblazer: the one who goes first and leads others in (2:10; 12:2).
The sacrifice that turns away God's wrath against sin (2:17). The same family of words as Romans 3:25, in your reading spine.

crossRefs.note: The backbone of the book: seated at the right hand, a priest forever.
The Word through whom all things were made.
The image of the invisible God, in whom all things hold together.
The wilderness generation that would not enter: the story behind Hebrews 3.

reflect: Hebrews 1:3 says Jesus sat down because the work was finished. Where am I still standing, trying to finish what he finished?
What is quietly crowding out the Word in my weeks right now (2:1)?
Who exhorts me every day, and whom do I exhort (3:13)?

practice.name: Consider Jesus
practice.how: Read Hebrews 3:1, 'consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession.' For ten minutes, do only that: write one line for each of the seven claims in 1:2-3, and thank him for each. Then send one brother one line of encouragement today (3:13).

pray: Adoration: the Son is the radiance of God's glory. Confession: where I have drifted or hardened my heart. Thanksgiving: he sat down; it is finished. Supplication: for one brother to exhort this week, and for a soft heart today.
journalPrompts: What did I learn about God this week, from the reading or from life?
Where did I see Jesus as better this week than the thing I was leaning on?
What question did this passage raise that I want to bring to my pastor or Micah?
